subject: WellSpring MAP: cost sanity checks, batching/caching assumptions and close timeline
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@wellspringhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@wellspringhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft + a couple quick cost questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the draft MAP — Elena here from WellSpring. Procurement asked me to pull one quick sanity check on your token economics before we circulate the MAP internally. Two quick asks:

1) You list ‘2.5K tokens / typical patient request’ in the eval profile — can you confirm what prompt/response split that assumes? (We typically see shorter prompts.)
2) Your cost example shows $0.004/token — is that pre- or post-batching/caching?

We want to get alignment on the baseline numbers before legal/procurement starts redlining the timeline. If you can drop a short note that calls out the assumptions (batch size, KV cache hit rate, quantization profile) that’d be super helpful.

Also attaching the procurement checklist for reference.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Clinical Integrations
WellSpring Health

Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@wellspringhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + a couple quick cost questions

Elena — thanks, good questions. High level answers up front, then I’ll loop in Marissa and Neha for the knobs and numbers: 

- The 2.5K tokens example is conservative and assumes: ~600-token prompt (multi-turn context + system instructions) with ~1.9K token generated output for a long form summarization use case. If your typical requests are shorter we should tighten this number.
- The $0.004/token in the doc was a list price equivalent for a large LLM variant before batching/caching savings. Real unit economics we use in MAPs show effective tokens/$ after our batching and KV caching applied.

Actionable next steps: Marissa — can you paste the MAP worksheet rows that show the per-request cost breakdown (tokens, model variant, batching factor, cache hit rate) so Elena and procurement can see the derivation? Neha — can you confirm safe conservative defaults for quantization and latency SLO impacts?

Proposed timeline: if we nail the numbers this week we can get procurement’s redlines by next Tue and aim for a signature by 6/30 — that’s the close window Elena mentioned on the call.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@wellspringhealth.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + a couple quick cost questions

Quick cost breakout (paste from MAP-WellSpring-v2.xlsx):

- Workload profile used: 60% short (<=512 tokens), 30% medium (512-2048), 10% long (>2048)
- Baseline tokens/request: 900 (prompt 350 / response 550) — conservative compared to your note; happy to re-run with your telemetry
- Model variant: rdx-large-v2 (FP16 quantized path)
- List price equivalent: $0.005/token
- Effective batching factor: 3.4 (this is the continuous-batching average we see for RLHF-style interactive workloads on your traffic shape)
- KV cache hit rate: assumed 18% (prefix reuse for repeat patient contexts)
- Resulting effective tokens/$: about 1,800 tokens per dollar (= tokens per dollar after batching & cache) — which maps to roughly $0.00056/token effective

Notes on sensitivity:
- If KV hit rate drops to 5%, cost per effective token increases ~12%.
- If batching factor is 2.0 instead of 3.4 (higher tail latency constraints), cost per token increases ~40%.

Attachment: MAP-WellSpring-v2.xlsx (contains tabbed calc + per-route rows)

Cc’ing Karthik to confirm queueing/batching tradeoffs if WellSpring needs tighter 95th%-ile latency guarantees.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@wellspringhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@wellspringhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-16T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + a couple quick cost questions

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement had two follow-ups after reviewing the MAP workbook:

1) They want a conservative ‘worst-case’ cost row (no KV cache + batching factor 1.2) so finance can model downside.
2) The SOC2 evidence request is live — procurement asked us to start the security questionnaire while pricing locks. Any chance you can provide the SOC2 evidence bundle and an estimated time to complete the questionnaire?

Timeline: legal is asking for a binding timeline for onboarding steps. Our internal target remains 6/30 signature but procurement indicated they may push to 7/14 if evidence/attestations take time. Can you confirm whether your team can produce the SOC2 evidence this week and a conservative close plan if we hit the 7/14 date?

Thanks — Elena

Attachment: SOC2-evidence-request.pdf (attachment stub)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena@wellspringhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@wellspringhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-17T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + a couple quick cost questions — final MAP rows and conservative plan

Elena / procurement team — final notes and next actions: 

1) Worst-case cost row: completed in MAP-WellSpring-v2.xlsx tab ‘Sensitivity’. Numbers shown assume batching factor 1.2 and 0% KV cache. That produces ~1,100 tokens/$ (vs the 1,800 optimistic above). We call that the Finance downside scenario.

2) SOC2 evidence: we can provide the standard SOC2 bundle (control descriptions, attestations, access logs summary) by EOD 6/18. Neha — can you confirm you’ll drop the evidence bundle link by tomorrow morning?

3) Conservative close path: if procurement needs more time, we propose a two-step agreement: (a) 6/30 — non-binding commercial terms + technical kickoff (sandbox access and eval quotas), (b) 7/14 — fully executed SOW with committed capacity. This keeps onboarding moving while procurement completes legal/SOC2 review.

4) Ask to WellSpring: please confirm the telemetry buckets (short/med/long) you expect us to use in the final MAP. If you can share a small sample of typical requests (anonymized), we’ll re-run the MAP numbers live and post updated per-route rows.

Links:
- Draft MAP and sensitivity table: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFGhI
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/WELL-2026-0432

Thanks — we’ll get the evidence bundle up and the conservative rows in the sheet by tomorrow. If those are green, I’ll coordinate a short procurement touchpoint early next week to close the loop on the timeline.

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
